_comment: Curated owner-language layer for version_history_build.py. Keyed by PR number in Xerialen/komodobots2. name = short display name; summary = jargon-free what-it-was-for; stamps = candidate_version stamps (prefix match) this merge shipped or governs — used to join bench margins and test-match counts.

31.name: Harvester & the dials
31.summary: Wrote down everything we learned from teaching the bots to pick up leftover weapons and packs (the harvester) and from tuning their behavior knobs (the dials): what was tried, what worked, and the reports behind it.

30.name: Pent-window rocket jump
30.summary: Measured how humans rocket-jump from the pent area up to the window on dm3, taken from real match demos, so the bots can learn the same shortcut.

28.name: Jump experiments E13/E14
28.summary: Documented two jump experiments on dm3 — the mirrored chain jump and the sng chain — with the evidence for what the bots can and cannot land.

27.name: Scratch runs don't block the bench
27.summary: Quick test matches no longer hold the lock that counted benchmark matches need, so both can run at the same time without stepping on each other.

23.name: Bench traffic control
23.summary: The bench now decides on its own how many matches can run at once without overloading the machine, so batches can be fired off without planning around each other.

18.name: Removed unused review machinery
18.summary: Deleted an automated code-review layer that was never used, to keep the project simple.

17.name: Speed-build idea disproven
17.summary: Tested the idea that building running speed before a fight would win more fights — it did not, so the movement work was parked with the evidence written down.

4.name: Bunnyhop theory
4.summary: Collected everything known about making the bots bunnyhop across our projects, why earlier attempts failed, and a plan for if we ever un-park it.

3.name: Pressure & flee-speed evidence
3.summary: Ran and recorded batches measuring how the bots behave under pressure and when fleeing, plus hardening of the match protocol.

2.name: The bench itself
2.summary: Built the local 4v4 benchmark: our bots vs stock frogbots on dm3, fully automated match running and scoring. Everything else is measured with this.

1.name: Program foundation
1.summary: Wrote the plan: what the project is trying to achieve (beat stock skill-20 frogbots convincingly), how progress is measured, and the roadmap.
